subject: AP preflight: payment options & vendor onboarding for Auricore
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Levine <sasha.levine@auricore.com>, Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@auricore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, May 2, 2027 at 3:10 PM PDT
Subject: AP preflight: payment options & vendor onboarding for Auricore

Hi Sasha / Jamal — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so your procurement team can triage: 

Key notes from discovery:
- Auricore has an internal AP gating rule: new vendor onboarding + vendor setup required for recurring contracts > $25k/year.
- Procurement prefers PO-based flows for vendor relationships but allows procurement card (P-Card) for pilot purchases up to an internal single-transaction limit (we discussed $25k as typical).
- Auricore is evaluating marketplace (AWS Marketplace) as an alternate route — faster net terms but needs a Redwood marketplace listing.

Options we can pursue (pros/cons & timelines):
1) Direct vendor onboarding (recommended for mid/long-term): vendor form + W9 + SOC2 --> PO issuance. Timeline ~ 3–6 weeks depending on legal/finance cycles.
2) P-Card for initial pilot: fastest path (~1–3 days) but single-transaction limit applies. Good for a short-term pilot or proof-of-value.
3) Marketplace subscription (Net30 via marketplace): faster procurement for customers already using marketplace procurement; requires Redwood listing and marketplace contract — timeline ~2 weeks after listing is live.

Attachments: vendor onboarding checklist and sample invoice attached.

Proposed next steps: 
- Sasha / Jamal: confirm whether your AP team can accept a P-Card for an initial pilot up to $25k and whether they require a PO for pilots > $5k (just to confirm thresholds).
- If PO required: attach your vendor onboarding packet or tell us the procurement form we should fill. We’ll start vendor onboarding in parallel while pilot runs on card (if allowed).
- I can join a short call with procurement to walk the onboarding checklist — available Tue/Thu morning PT.

Thanks — I’ll await your confirmation and any procurement contact info if different from procurement@auricore.com.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- redwood-sample-invoice.pdf (PDF)

From: Sasha Levine <sasha.levine@auricore.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jamal Ortiz <jamal.ortiz@auricore.com>, procurement@auricore.com
Date: Mon, May 3, 2027 at 09:08 AM PDT
Subject: Re: AP preflight: payment options & vendor onboarding for Auricore

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Confirmed: Procurement requires vendor setup for any vendor invoices that are recurring or expected to exceed $25k annually.
- For pilots, our P-Card desk can approve single transactions up to $30k but we need an internal justification and PO is preferred above $10k in some BU cases.
- Marketplace is attractive but leadership wants to avoid additional vendor consolidation unless it shortens time-to-value. If Redwood is already on AWS Marketplace that would help.

I'll pull in the procurement admin if you can share the completed onboarding checklist and SOC2 link.

Sasha Levine
Head of Partnerships
Auricore Health

Subject: Re: AP preflight: payment options & vendor onboarding for Auricore

Appreciate the clarity, Sasha — glad the P-Card ceiling is flexible. To make procurement's life easier, here are two pragmatic paths we recommend so you can start an evaluation quickly: 

A) Fast pilot + vendor setup in parallel (recommended):
- Start pilot on P-Card (single payment up to $30k) while we submit the vendor package to your AP team.
- We’ll provide: completed vendor onboarding checklist, W9, SOC2 link, customer reference, and a sample invoice.
- If pilot expands beyond pilot threshold, AP can convert to PO-based recurring agreement without interruption.
Timeline: pilot charged in <1 week; vendor setup 3–6 weeks.

B) Marketplace route (if you prefer central procurement via marketplace):
- We can accelerate an AWS Marketplace listing conversation but listing takes coordination across procurement/legal on both sides.
- Marketplace gives Net30 and consolidated billing — timeline ~2 weeks post-listing readiness.

Ask from you: please confirm the BU threshold where you’d insist on a PO vs card (you mentioned $10k in some BU cases). Also share the procurement admin contact and the vendor form (if different from procurement@auricore.com).

I attached a one-page SOW draft that maps the pilot deliverables and pricing to help your internal justification. If helpful, I can join a short call with your procurement admin this week — Tue/Thu mornings PT are open for me.

—Karthik
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs):
- auricore-pilot-scope.docx (SOW draft)
- redwood_vendor_onboarding_checklist.xlsx

Karthik — thanks for laying out options and the SOW. Quick answers from procurement: 
- We can greenlight a P-Card transaction up to $25k for the pilot (we'll route approval through the P-Card desk).
- Anything expected to be recurring or > $25k/year will require vendor onboarding + PO.
- Please send completed onboarding checklist, W9, and SOC2 link to procurement@auricore.com and cc me.

Let's do a 20-minute call tomorrow (Thu May 5) at 10:30 AM ET to fast-track vendor form questions and confirm payment routing. Can Karthik or Marissa join?

Thanks,
Jamal Ortiz
Director, Procurement
Auricore Health
